video_title: Stephen Jackson tells all about his INFAMOUS "O'BLOCK visit" 👀

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: How Tony Allen changed the narrative about visiting Memphis neighborhoods
quotes.excerpt: When guys like you go over there, you change the narrative.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: When I saw you out there, I knew you were in good hands. I knew no one was going to touch you. That is the criticism Memphis is getting out back in the day. We were shy-racking and all that. When guys like you go over there, you change the narrative. You change not only that, guys who could get hope. When you came over there with the stereotypical ideas that everybody got from not wanting to go over there, you changed that.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: No, we are not trying to rob you. No, we are not trying to take nothing for you. But little Ray-Ray over there, Stephen Jackson made it believable you can come over there.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Tony Allen explains the backstory of his O'Block visit
quotes.excerpt: I went to O'Block because I can. Y'all just can't.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: I never, the only reason I am talking about it is because your people are the reason why I went over there. So it is about 2:00, 3:00 in the morning, bro. We had a big three game. We drunk than a skunk. We sitting in the lobby, my drunk ass. Shout out PT. Let's go to O'Block. PT like, you want to go for real? I am like, yeah, nigga. Man, let's go to O'Block. He made the call. They like, pull up. I went to O'Block because I can. Y'all just can't.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Summer time, hold on man. Summer time.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Tony Allen reflects on his relationship with the youth in O'Block
quotes.excerpt: We understand they make the mistakes trying to survive. They really got good hearts, bro.
quotes.quote: I go out there late night with my weed. I go out there, roll, shoot some hoops, fucking with the youngsters. I meet a youngster, me and him stay in contact. He end up getting shot, I end up looking out for him, you know what I am saying, trying to pull him out, give him a job, even call him, try to give him a job. And end up building a relationship with, I think God, that was God, you know what I am saying, because I was really trying to help him. Like I really fuck with him. Like he really a good kid. But we understand they make the mistakes trying to survive. They really got good hearts, bro. They just trying to survive and they no blueprint to this shit.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph on the importance of providing hope to at-risk youth
quotes.excerpt: Juwan Howard did it to me. Came back, laid the payment and gave me hope.
quotes.quote: When you did that, I want to put this in perspective too. When you did that, man, you know how many times, me coming from and living in those, I grew up on 95th, Prince of Peace, Lathrop Homes is the projects, right? When I used to, when I got drafted, bro, I am telling you some weird, crazy shit. I used to go to New York, bro, and just drag in my driver to drive me through those projects and just see like, damn, Chicago going on in New York. New York going on in, everywhere. Port Arthur going on in Marion. It is all the same. We come from the same environments. These are the type of cats that is like, damn, I made it, but I still got to go get some more folks some hope. Juwan Howard did it to me. You hear me? Juwan Howard did it to me, came back, laid the payment and gave me hope.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph on the impact of positive presence in tough neighborhoods
quotes.excerpt: You being over there maybe could have been the halt to a whole lot of other stuff.
quotes.quote: Will Bynum was with us. So it is like, bro, when you hit the, the naysayers, bro. Bro, continue being a real one with those. You got more love, you got more love than haters. All, there is more players than haters in this world what we do anyway. You being over there maybe could have been the halt to a whole lot of other stuff, just by you being over there. Them, them folks over there probably could have been going to slide. You probably changed their mind. Hold on, now let's kick it, Stack Jack right here. You don't know just by your presence and being right there, changed a whole lot of people perspectives on just the, the whatever they think about stars or fame or whatever the case may be.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Tony Allen on the impact of T Grizzley's prison outreach
quotes.excerpt: T Grizzley go to prisons and speak to the youth.
quotes.quote: And you know what made me feel good too, Z-Bo, like this, this how things come back around. So, we got T Grizzley on the show. T Grizzley go to prisons and speak to the youth. The little homie that I met, got up and told T Grizzley, man, Stephen Jackson, the room, he looked out for me, bro. I got, you know what I am saying? As soon as I see, he was like, T Grizzley came like, bro, I know you don't know, but the nigga you talking about in Chicago, because I saw you set on the show, he said I talked to him. He said you a real one for that. You know what I am saying? So like, shit like that, I do that everywhere. But I don't do it for, for props. I am just a solid dude, bro. I don't do it for attention.
